john_cust: Hey, getting a Pydantic validation error when using JSON mode with streaming responses. Worked previously, started failing after last runtime bump. Payload says 'Expecting value' from our consumer.
lee_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw stream or a repro? quickest is a curl or a small snippet.
john_cust: Repro attached — streaming endpoint. We just pass prompt + "structured_output: json". Here's the last few chunks we received (concatenated):
```
{"id": "123", "items": [
  {"name": "a", "score": 0.9},
  {"name": "b", "score": 0.8},
]}
{"id": "124", "items": [
  {"name": "c", "score": 0.95}
]}
```
This causes json.loads to blow up — trailing comma + two top-level objects concatenated. Our Pydantic model expects a single object so validation fails.
lee_support: Looks like two issues: (1) trailing comma in first object, (2) multiple JSON objects in a single stream. Do you get these as separate event/frame boundaries from the runtime or already concatenated by your http client?
john_cust: We receive them as separate SSE chunks. Our client concatenates chunks and calls pydantic.parse_raw on the final buffer. Sometimes the runtime emits partial punctuation in chunk A and the rest in chunk B, but here it looks like two complete objects were sent back-to-back.
ingrid_eng: @lee_support @ryan_ml tagging eng-ml — this smells like the generator emitted two objects because of a bug in the structured-output postprocessing. I can repro locally by simulating streaming with our JSON serializer + deterministic batching. Repro steps:
1) run curl against /v1/generate with header `Accept: text/event-stream` and body: `{"mode": "json", "prompt": "..."}`
2) capture SSE payloads (they come in separate data: frames)
3) combine frames naïvely and attempt to parse with json.loads -> fails when generator yields two envelope objects without a comma or top-level array.

Short log excerpt: `2026-03-02T12:02:03Z runtime: emitted JSON_OBJECT_END` then `2026-03-02T12:02:03Z runtime: emitted JSON_OBJECT_START` without an intervening separator.
ryan_ml: I ran the same and also saw trailing commas emitted when tokenization cutoff hit after an array element. Two failure modes: incomplete chunking (split tokens create invalid JSON across chunks) and multiple objects emitted when the model/decoder restarts envelope emission between examples.
lee_support: For a workaround, if you control the client: instead of parse_raw on the naive concatenation, treat the stream as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or parse objects incrementally (e.g., ijson or json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode loop) to recover multiple objects. That avoids the trailing-comma issue because you parse as you go.
john_cust: Ok will try incremental decode. Is this something you can fix on the runtime side? We expect the runtime to emit a single well-formed JSON envelope for structured_output mode.
ingrid_eng: We're escalating. Short-term runtime fix: ensure the postprocessor serializes a single top-level array/object and buffers until the envelope is complete before emitting the final data event. Longer-term: change generator to avoid trailing commas and to emit explicit SSE events with type: 'json-chunk' plus a final 'json-end' signal.
ryan_ml: Also adding a guard in the validation layer to detect multiple top-level objects and return an explicit error code (400-ish) that the SDK can map to a deterministic retry/assembly strategy.
lee_support: @john_cust reproducer would help — can you share the exact curl and a link to the small logfile? If you prefer, we can take your account logs and attach to the ticket (we'll redact PII).
john_cust: Uploaded logs to the ticket and included curl. Thanks — trying incremental parse now.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: CI run for patch branch runtime/jsonstream-buffering passed (build 2117).
lee_support: Internal note: tagging this high priority because it causes customer-facing Pydantic validation noise and blocks ingestion workflows. Escalated to eng-ml on call. Will follow up when we have a runtime patch.
ryan_ml: Quick patch plan posted to the eng-ml channel — we'll try a 1-line guard + integration test for NDJSON vs single-envelope. ETA for canary: tomorrow.
lee_support: Thanks all :thumbsup: john_cust — keep us posted if incremental parsing works, otherwise we'll fast-track a patch to your org's dedicated runtime override.
john_cust: Incremental parser worked around it for now. Appreciate the fast triage.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread about structured output JSON mode streaming parse failures and schema validation integration (Pydantic/JSON). No nested JSON fields allowed per dataset rules.
